# Setting up a new repository

Read the `housing` and `commit-rules` skills first; this skill puts the steps in order and lists what agents have
missed. A good model of a small shared library is `/cosmoshot/model-runtime`; of an experiment, `/cosmoshot/lipsync`.

## 1. Decide before you create

- **Does it exist already?** Search before you build: `cosmo-mem find "<topic>" --cwd .`, `grep -rIl <name> /cosmoshot/*/README.md`,
  and the older code under `/srv`. Another team may hold the same code (lipsync's agent found that Sonalon had already ported it).
- **A small place needs no name.** An experiment, a one-off or a small library is a repository with an owning team, not a new
  team: it gets no `who` name, no board project and no new memory store. Its owner is an existing team, written in its
  `AGENTS.md`. Something that grows an agent of its own, a board name or its own memory is a team or a project: use the
  `new-team` skill instead.
- **Owner.** One team owns the repository (plc, cosmogenitor, sonalon, ...). The owner is a team, never the library.
  Pick the board project that fits (`program`, `cosmogenitor`, `sonalon`, `plc`, `cyberplanetary`, `platform`; there is
  no way to add one). Memory access follows that project: a session reads `program` and its own store and writes only its own.
- **Name.** `/cosmoshot/<name>` is the working copy and `cosmoshot/<name>` the GitLab path; one name for both.
- **Shared library?** Code that two or more applications use unchanged is one component with one owner, published as a
  versioned package and vendored read-only by the others (`/cosmoshot/tools/docs/VENDORING.md`). Code one application uses
  stays in that application.
- **Board.** The board does not know about repositories. For work other teams depend on, or a shared library, create one board
  task (record what you do as notes on it, with `X-Actor` and note `author` set to your team, as the `board` skill says): `who` is the owning team (never invent a name: the API refuses names outside its
  list of 15), a project from the six, `high_priority` stated, and an objective (a shared library serves O162). Create one tag
  for the library, for example `lib: model-runtime`, so everything about it can be found together. An experiment nobody
  depends on may have no task if its owner chooses so; say that in its `AGENTS.md`.

## 2. Create the files

In `/cosmoshot/<name>`: `git init -b main`, then:

- `LICENSE` (the programme default is AGPL-3.0: copy it from `/cosmoshot/model-runtime`), `README.md`.
- `AGENTS.md` (a few lines: what this is, the owner, the commands) and `CLAUDE.md` containing exactly `@AGENTS.md`. Do not
  write the "Working in the Cosmoshot programme" block yourself: step 4 fills it.
- `program.json` with `{"owner": "<owning team>"}`, so its sessions get that team's messages (step 4).
- `docs/HOUSING.md`: where the repository lives, what is kept out of git, where its second copy is, and what a fresh clone needs.
- `PROVENANCE.md` and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` if you bring in outside code, with each licence.
- Large or unversioned files go in `/cosmoshot/store/<name>/` (a link to the big disk), with a second copy under
  `/media/Vivarium/cosmoshot/<name>/`; write both in `docs/HOUSING.md`. Never put them in git or under `/tmp`.
- No credentials in any file. `.commitlintrc.cjs` and `.gitlint` are written by the git template: do not add them.

## 3. Commit and push

- Commit message: `type(scope): text`, text lower-case, a blank line, a body, every line under 100 characters, no trailers,
  no email addresses (the `commit-rules` skill). The hook rejects anything else, so check with `git log -1 --format=%B`.
- The remote is `ssh://git@gitlab.benac.dev:32224/cosmoshot/<name>.git` (this exact shape, port 32224).
  `git remote add origin <that> && git push --no-verify -u origin main` creates the project. Push `main` first, then look at
  the project's default branch: it has not always been `main`.
- Agents hold no GitLab API token and must not mint one (`/srv/praxes/gitlab/credentials-for-agents.md`). The API goes
  through devops' broker, which keeps the credential and logs who asked: `/usr/bin/python3
  /cosmoshot/tools/ops/gitlab_broker.py ask <action> --project cosmoshot/<name> --team <team> --session <id>
  --task T<n> [--param k=v] [--apply]`. Actions: project.read, project.set_description (needs
  `--param if_match.description_sha=<sha256 of the current description>`), mirror.status, mr.create, mr.read,
  group.projects, lease.acquire, lease.release. A write is a dry run until `--apply`. Runbook:
  `/cosmoshot/tools/docs/GITLAB-BROKER.md`. Protecting `main` (main.protect, main.restore) is devops only: for a new
  repository ask devops on a board task to run main.protect (force-push and deletion are blocked; direct pushes work).
- Push-to-create works because the machine's ssh key is registered; do not look for a token. On the first push a machine hook
  adds a semantic-release bootstrap commit, so the first `git pull --rebase` afterwards is not optional (it also applies to
  later pushes to `main`).

## 4. Register it, so it gets the shared skills

- Add `{"name": "<name>", "path": "/cosmoshot/<name>"}` to `repositories` in `/cosmoshot/skills/sources/projects/<project>.json`
  for the owner's project: one small commit, `git pull --rebase` first, push as in `commit-rules`. Without this the
  repository gets no skills, no memory note and no managed `AGENTS.md` block.
- Then the 15-minute rollout writes the block, `CLAUDE.md` and the skills into the repository; to see it sooner run
  `/usr/bin/python3 generate.py plan` from `/cosmoshot/skills`. One writer per repository: never run a script that rewrites
  many repositories at once, and never edit the managed block by hand.
- A repository under `/cosmoshot` is in the `program` memory project unless devops adds a path prefix for it in
  `/cosmoshot/tools/projects.json`; a small place stays there.
- Messages and the message hook reach a session by its folder's team. A new folder is in no team, so put a `program.json`
  at the repository root naming the owner by board name: `{"owner": "<owning team>"}` (for example `aiofourown`); it is
  committed with the repository, and no request to devops is needed. An unknown owner or a broken file gives no team and
  breaks nothing. Board notices go by the task's `who`, not by folder. Send with `--from <that team's cosmo-msg name>`, never
  an invented sender: replies go to the sender name, and only a team name can receive them.
- Names are matched as plain string prefixes: do not name a repository as an extension of another (`xxx-site`, `xxx2`) unless it
  should belong to `xxx`: `privatelocalchat-site` is in the `plc` project and team because of its prefix.

## 5. If it publishes or goes public

- A package is published with `/cosmoshot/tools/ops/forge_package.py` by the owner; consumers pin the exact version and its
  SHA-256 (`VENDORING.md`).
- A public mirror is listed in `/cosmoshot/tools/ops/forge-mirrors.json` and mirrored by devops; note it in `docs/HOUSING.md`.
- `cyberplanetary-*` repositories also push to the Forge (see `commit-rules`).

## Check before you say it is done

    git -C /cosmoshot/<name> status -sb        # level with origin, clean apart from .commitlintrc.cjs and .gitlint
    git -C /cosmoshot/<name> remote -v         # origin is the ssh:// cosmoshot URL
    ls /media/Vivarium/cosmoshot/<name>        # the second copy of the store exists (easy to forget)
    cat /cosmoshot/<name>/program.json         # the owner is a board team name
    ls /cosmoshot/<name>/.claude/skills        # the skills arrived (after the rollout)
